target_profile.system_boundary: hashicorp/raft is an embeddable Go library implementing a single Raft consensus group whose replicated state is an application FSM; the library owns leadership/election, log replication, commitment, membership, snapshots and the FSM application loop, while the application owns the FSM, the LogStore/StableStore/SnapshotStore and the Transport (inmem, tcp or network).
protocol_contexts: Leader appends client commands and replicates them to followers (A1).
Followers/candidates/leaders maintain term and leadership context (A2).
Membership configuration (voter/nonvoter) determines quorum and eligibility (A4).
Committed entries are applied to the FSM (A5).
ownership: Per-instance: each Raft object owns its own raftState, configurations, stable store view and leaderState.
Per-term leadership: leaderState (commitment, inflight, replState, notify) is created on becoming leader and destroyed on step-down.
Transport-owned: the network layer decides whether a request is delivered on the main loop or through the optional heartbeat fast path.
selection_injection: The application selects log/stable/snapshot stores, transport, FSM and timeouts via Config.
BatchApplyCh and MaxAppendEntries control group-commit batching.
PreVoteDisabled and transport support select pre-vote behaviour.
variants: BatchingFSM vs single-entry FSM; ConfigurationStore present or not.
inmem vs tcp vs network transport (only the network transport installs the heartbeat fast path).

activities.purpose: Qualified support for decision formation and legal advancement: a leader's new entries advance to committed and then to the FSM only when a quorum of the current voter set has stored them.
activities.realization_summary: Raft.dispatchLogs writes entries to the local LogStore and marks them inflight; one followerReplication goroutine per peer ships AppendEntries and reports the follower's match index; commitment.match/recalculate advance commitIndex under the term-start-index rule; the leaderLoop commit path applies the committed prefix.
variants: snapshot replication when the entry is compacted away

activities.purpose: Context validity and acquisition, transfer or loss of authority: terms, votes, the leader role and its removal, including leadership transfer.
activities.realization_summary: Followers time out heartbeats and become candidates; candidates pre-vote (optionally), increment and persist the term, request votes and win on a quorum; voters decide with term, log up-to-date-ness, prior-vote and configuration checks; leaders step down on newer terms or lease loss; a leader can hand over via TimeoutNow.
unknowns: Whether the (setState, setCurrentTerm) pair in appendEntries can be observed as a term regression by an external reader when the off-thread heartbeat path runs concurrently with a campaign is not established.

activities.purpose: Recovery and resynchronization of eligible participation when a follower is too far behind to replay the log.
activities.realization_summary: The leader ships the newest snapshot when setPreviousLog cannot read the leader's next-1 entry; the follower installs it into the SnapshotStore, restores the FSM, resets lastApplied/lastSnapshot and adopts the snapshot configuration.

activities.purpose: Configuration and participant eligibility: which servers exist, which have votes, and therefore what a quorum is.
activities.realization_summary: Membership changes are encoded as LogConfiguration/LogRemovePeerDeprecated entries; latest/committed configurations are tracked separately; replication goroutines are started and stopped to match; hasVote/quorumSize derive eligibility and quorum from the latest configuration.

activities.purpose: Decision application and consumption: committed entries reach the application FSM exactly once and in order.
activities.realization_summary: Raft.runFSM consumes fsmMutateCh batches, dispatches LogCommand/LogBarrier/LogConfiguration, updates lastIndex/lastTerm and resolves the associated futures.

activities.purpose: History, persistence and reconstruction of the support that authority and commitment rely on.
activities.realization_summary: CurrentTerm, LastVoteTerm and LastVoteCand are written to StableStore before being relied on; the log and snapshots provide the prefix; NewRaft reloads term and scans configuration entries at startup.

activities.purpose: Client contracts, invocation intervals and observed completion: how callers submit work and learn whether it was applied.
activities.realization_summary: Apply/ApplyLog/Barrier enqueue logFutures onto applyCh with an optional enqueue timeout; VerifyLeader uses verifyCh; futures are resolved exactly once through deferError.respond, or answered with ErrNotLeader/ErrLeadershipLost/ErrRaftShutdown/ErrAbortedByRestore.

behaviors.execution_owner: Raft.dispatchLogs, executed on the leader main loop
behaviors.protocol_context: Leader turns an accepted client command/barrier/no-op or configuration request into local log entries for the current term.
behaviors.trigger: leaderLoop receives entries from applyCh (group-commit batch), or runLeader/appendConfigurationEntry dispatches a no-op/configuration entry.
legal_preconditions: server is Leader for its current term
no leadership transfer is in progress
not in the middle of stepping down after self-removal
implementation_guards: ErrLeadershipTransferInProgress rejects new applies while a transfer is running
the stepDown flag responds ErrNotLeader instead of dispatching once the leader has removed itself
writes: commitment.matchIndexes for the local server via match(localID)
durable_effects: entries are persisted with StoreLogs before any acknowledgement or replication
important_branches: StoreLogs failure logs, answers every future with the error and sets state Follower
async_boundaries: each followerReplication is notified through asyncNotifyCh(triggerCh) rather than being called directly

cross_activity_effects.A6: the entry becomes durable history before it can be counted toward a quorum

existing_protections: local persistence happens before the local match index is reported to commitment

behaviors.execution_owner: Raft.replicate/replicateTo plus one followerReplication goroutine per peer
behaviors.protocol_context: A leader drives each peer's log toward its own by sending AppendEntries, or a snapshot when the needed entry is gone.
behaviors.trigger: triggerCh when new entries are dispatched, triggerDeferErrorCh for leadership transfer, a random CommitTimeout tick, and stopCh when the peer leaves the configuration.
legal_preconditions: the sending server still believes it is leader for s.currentTerm
implementation_guards: a response with resp.Term > req.Term stops replication and signals step-down through handleStaleTerm
rejected AppendEntries move nextIndex back with backoff
ErrLogNotFound switches to snapshot transfer
reads: follower last log index from the response
external_effects: the follower stores or replaces its log suffix
important_branches: pipeline mode is attempted after a success and falls back to the sequential path on any error
a successful response only records a match up to the last entry actually sent
async_boundaries: runs in its own goroutine; commitment.match is the only shared hand-off back to the leader loop

cross_activity_effects.A3: either replay the log or fall back to shipping a snapshot

existing_protections: the follower's reject response steers the leader to an earlier entry instead of overwriting unvalidated history

behaviors.protocol_context: The leader tracks, per voter of the latest configuration, the highest log index that voter is known to hold, and derives commitIndex as the quorum match index.
behaviors.trigger: match() calls from the local dispatch path and from successful AppendEntries responses.
legal_preconditions: the server is leader and the commitment struct exists for this term
implementation_guards: only voters of the latest configuration have entries in matchIndexes
an index below startIndex (the first index appended in this term) can never be committed
important_branches: setConfiguration rebuilds matchIndexes on a membership change and immediately recalculates
recalculate is a no-op while the match index map is empty
async_boundaries: notifies the leader loop by a buffered channel, never by calling into it

cross_activity_effects.A4: the voter set used for quorum is the latest configuration, which may still be uncommitted

existing_protections: the startIndex rule prevents a new leader from committing entries left by an earlier term on the strength of its own election

the configuration-change gate admits a new change only while latestIndex equals committedIndex, and nextConfiguration applies a single server change, so at most one uncommitted single-server change is in flight and any majority of the new voter set intersects every majority of the committed voter set
unknowns: Whether the majority-intersection reasoning covers every permitted sequence of one-at-a-time changes is not established by execution; reading only shows that at most one uncommitted change is admitted.

behaviors.protocol_context: When the quorum match index advances, the leader publishes a new commit index, commits a pending configuration, and applies the newly committed prefix.
legal_preconditions: still Leader when the notification is processed
implementation_guards: only inflight entries with index <= commitIndex are removed and applied
a committed configuration that no longer contains the leader sets stepDown
important_branches: with ShutdownOnRemove the leader shuts down instead of transitioning to Follower after removing itself
async_boundaries: committed batches are handed to the FSM goroutine through fsmMutateCh; futures are answered there

cross_activity_effects.A4: commits the pending configuration and can remove the leader itself
cross_activity_effects.A5: enqueues the committed prefix for FSM application

existing_protections: application to the FSM is bounded by commitIndex, so uncommitted entries are never applied

behaviors.execution_owner: Raft.appendEntries, executed on the main loop for normal RPCs and through the transport heartbeat fast path for pure heartbeats
behaviors.protocol_context: A server receives an AppendEntries request from a server claiming leadership and reconciles its term, believed leader, log suffix, commit index and configuration.
behaviors.trigger: an AppendEntriesRequest carrying entries, a commit index advance, or only a heartbeat
implementation_guards: requests with a.Term < currentTerm are ignored
a.Term > currentTerm, or any request while not Follower (unless this node is campaigning from a leadership transfer), forces a transition to Follower
entries are accepted only if PrevLogEntry/PrevLogTerm match the local log or snapshot
a conflicting entry term clears the local suffix with DeleteRange
writes: commitIndex and configurations.latest on configuration entries
durable_effects: append/delete of log entries in the LogStore
important_branches: when a truncation passes a configuration index, the latest configuration falls back to the committed one
a commit index advance applies entries up to min(leaderCommit, local last index)

the transport fast path carries only pure heartbeats (nonzero term, no previous entry, no entries, zero leader commit index), so that off-thread invocation takes no log, configuration or commit branch

the transport's handling of that fast path waits for the response channel or its own shutdown with no deadline, so when the node has shut down but its transport is still open the dropped heartbeat parks that connection's handler goroutine until the transport itself stops
async_boundaries: the FSM application is again deferred to the FSM goroutine through processLogs

cross_activity_effects.A1: the prefix check and suffix replacement are what make a follower's match index meaningful support
cross_activity_effects.A6: appends and deletions are durable log history

existing_protections: the PrevLogEntry/PrevLogTerm check refuses to append behind a mismatch, and NoRetryBackoff tells the leader to regress cheaply

every field a pure heartbeat touches is individually serialized: state and currentTerm are atomic in raftState, leaderAddr/leaderID use leaderLock, lastContact uses lastContactLock, and observe takes a read lock

an exploration observed that while the node runs the same heartbeat call is answered immediately, whereas after a clean shutdown the same call returned without answering within the observation window, so the shutdown branch drops the request instead of responding
unknowns: The (setState, setCurrentTerm) pair in appendEntries is not atomic as a pair, so an off-thread heartbeat and a concurrent campaign can still interleave at the field level; whether an external reader can observe a term regression is not established.

behaviors.protocol_context: A follower that stops hearing from a leader becomes willing to campaign.
behaviors.trigger: the follower's heartbeat timer fires and LastContact is older than HeartbeatTimeout
legal_preconditions: the node is in the Follower state
implementation_guards: no election is started when no configuration is known
no election is started when the latest configuration is identical to the committed one and the local node is not a voter
only a voter transitions to Candidate
important_branches: a non-voter or a node outside the stable configuration only warns instead of campaigning
async_boundaries: returns to Raft.run, which re-enters runCandidate
existing_protections: a node that is not a current voter of a stable configuration refuses to disturb the cluster

behaviors.execution_owner: Raft.runCandidate with Raft.electSelf (and Raft.preElectSelf for the pre-vote round)
behaviors.protocol_context: A candidate proposes the next term and tries to win a quorum of votes.
behaviors.trigger: the server enters the Candidate state after a heartbeat/election timeout or a TimeoutNow request
legal_preconditions: the server is a voter of the latest configuration
implementation_guards: pre-vote is attempted first unless disabled or this is a leadership-transfer campaign
a response or pre-vote with a newer term drops the campaign back to Follower
votes needed is quorumSize() over the latest configuration voters
the leadership-transfer flag is reset when the campaign ends
durable_effects: CurrentTerm and the self vote in StableStore
external_effects: RequestVote/RequestPreVote RPCs to every other voter
important_branches: if persisting the self vote fails, electSelf returns a nil channel and the campaign makes no further progress this round
pre-vote reaching a quorum resets the timer and starts the real election
async_boundaries: each vote request runs in its own goroutine and reports back on a buffered channel

cross_activity_effects.A6: the term is persisted before it is used to request votes

existing_protections: a higher term observed at any point aborts the campaign
votes are counted only from voters of the latest configuration

behaviors.protocol_context: A server decides whether to grant its vote for a term to the candidate that requested it.
behaviors.trigger: a RequestVoteRequest is processed on the main loop
implementation_guards: a candidate outside the configuration or without a vote is rejected
a request is rejected when a different leader is known, unless the candidate set the LeadershipTransfer flag
an older term is rejected and a newer term makes the server step down and adopt it
the candidate's last log term/index must be at least as up to date as the local last entry
a repeated request for the same term is granted only to the same candidate
durable_effects: the granted vote is persisted before responding
important_branches: a request from a non-voter with a higher term still updates the term and steps down but is denied
existing_protections: the persisted per-term vote is what stops two leaders from being elected in one term

behaviors.protocol_context: An optional pre-election round that asks whether a campaign would succeed before any term is incremented.
behaviors.trigger: a candidate starts a campaign with a pre-vote-capable transport, or a RequestPreVoteRequest arrives
legal_preconditions: the transport implements WithPreVote and PreVoteDisabled is false
implementation_guards: no state or term change is made in either the request handler or the requester
non-voters and known-leader situations are rejected as in a real vote
the candidate's last log entry is compared for up-to-date-ness
important_branches: a transport that answers 'unexpected command' is treated as granting the pre-vote so the cluster can still progress
async_boundaries: pre-vote responses are tallied on the candidate main loop
existing_protections: avoiding a term increment unless a quorum would vote for the candidate

a pre-vote round changes no state and winning it only starts a real election, which still requires a majority of the latest configuration's votes under the same membership, prior-vote and log-up-to-dateness checks
unknowns: Whether an inflated pre-vote tally in a mixed-version cluster (a peer without the pre-vote RPC is counted as granting) causes avoidable election churn is not established; the pre-vote itself grants nothing.

behaviors.execution_owner: Raft.checkLeaderLease, Raft.handleStaleTerm and the Raft.runLeader deferred cleanup
behaviors.protocol_context: A leader abandons the role when it can no longer support it, and the term/authority it held stops being usable.
behaviors.trigger: the leader lease timer fires, a follower replies with a newer term, or a request with a newer term arrives; leadership is also lost through the leadershipTransfer/LostLeadership paths
implementation_guards: lease contact is counted only over voters of the latest configuration
contacted < quorumSize() forces the step-down
a self-removal via a committed configuration also forces the step-down
external_effects: pending verify requests answered with ErrLeadershipLost
important_branches: on step-down all inflight log futures fail, so a caller cannot mistake an uncommitted write for an applied one
async_boundaries: stepDown is signalled from replication goroutines through a buffered channel

cross_activity_effects.A1: destroying the commitment struct stops this server from advancing commitIndex for its old term

existing_protections: the lease check counts only current voters, so an unreachable quorum removes the leader

behaviors.protocol_context: A leader deliberately hands authority to another voter without waiting for a timeout.
behaviors.trigger: LeadershipTransfer/LeadershipTransferToServer, or a TimeoutNowRequest on the target
legal_preconditions: the server is Leader; the target is a voter with replication state
implementation_guards: leadership transfer replicates up to the leader's last index before sending TimeoutNow
only one transfer may be in progress
the target records that its campaign came from a transfer so the old leader's heartbeats do not immediately demote it
important_branches: the transfer reports nil once leadership is lost, and an error after an ElectionTimeout if the target does not take over
async_boundaries: the transfer runs in its own goroutine while the leader loop keeps serving; while it runs, applies and configuration changes are rejected

cross_activity_effects.A1: the handover first pushes the target's log to the leader's last index so no committed entry is stranded

existing_protections: the target ignores the outgoing leader's heartbeats only for its transfer campaign, and the flag is cleared when the campaign ends
the receiver's campaign still needs a majority of the latest configuration's real votes, so a TimeoutNow that is not checked against the sender or the current term can at most start an election round
unknowns: Whether a non-leader or stale peer can use TimeoutNow to cause repeated election rounds is not established; the request's term and sender are not consulted.

behaviors.protocol_context: A lagging server is resynchronized by transferring the leader's newest snapshot instead of replaying compacted entries.
behaviors.trigger: the leader cannot read entry nextIndex-1, or an InstallSnapshotRequest arrives, or a snapshot exists at startup
legal_preconditions: a snapshot with a supported version exists
implementation_guards: snapshot versions outside [min,max] are rejected
an InstallSnapshot with an older term is ignored
the received byte count must equal the announced size
durable_effects: the snapshot is written to the SnapshotStore
external_effects: the FSM is restored from the snapshot
important_branches: a snapshot carries the configuration at its index, and that configuration becomes latest and committed on the follower
async_boundaries: restore is performed by the FSM goroutine through fsmMutateCh

cross_activity_effects.A1: provides a consistent log/snapshot starting point for further replication

existing_protections: the snapshot is only accepted after the whole payload is verified and the FSM restore succeeds

behaviors.protocol_context: The leader changes cluster membership or suffrage by appending a configuration entry and matching the replication set to it.
behaviors.trigger: a configurationChangeFuture is accepted once the latest configuration is committed and this leader has committed an entry of its term
implementation_guards: prevIndex rejects a change computed against a superseded configuration
at most one uncommitted configuration is produced by gating on latestIndex == committedIndex
durable_effects: the configuration entry is written to the log
external_effects: replication goroutines are started or stopped
important_branches: removed peers are asked to replicate up to the current last index before replication stops

when dispatchLogs reports a StoreLogs failure it answers the future with that error and sets state Follower, but appendConfigurationEntry still publishes the new configuration through setLatestConfiguration(configuration, future.Index()) and recomputes commitment.setConfiguration for the new voter set

a node that adopted such an unpersisted configuration can campaign under it because latestIndex differs from committedIndex, a fresh peer with an empty configuration can supply the missing vote, and the leader commit path then promotes the adopted configuration to committed once its index falls within the commit index, without consulting the entry stored at that index

the configuration is not stored separately from the log: a restart over identical stores re-derives it by scanning configuration entries, so a configuration whose entry was never written does not survive the restart

cross_activity_effects.A1: changes the voter set that the commitment quorum is computed over

existing_protections: the change is only applied once the previous configuration is committed, preserving the one-uncommitted-configuration rule
the failed write is surfaced to the requesting caller as an error future, so the caller is not told that the change was applied
recovery reads configuration state only from stored entries, so the in-memory adoption is confined to the running instance
unknowns: Whether an application FSM that applied entries under the in-memory configuration is consistent with the configuration re-derived after a restart is not established.

behaviors.protocol_context: Committed entries are handed to the application FSM in batches and the associated futures are resolved.
behaviors.trigger: a batch of commitTuple values arrives on fsmMutateCh
legal_preconditions: the entries were admitted by processLogs up to the leader's commitIndex
implementation_guards: only LogCommand/LogBarrier/LogConfiguration are handled; unknown types panic in prepareLog
LogConfiguration reaches the FSM only when the FSM implements ConfigurationStore
important_branches: a BatchingFSM receives only command/configuration entries while barrier futures are still answered
async_boundaries: runs on its own goroutine, serialized by fsmMutateCh
existing_protections: single-threaded application order prevents concurrent Apply calls

the FSM receives only entries admitted up to the commit index, and a committed entry is not truncated because an elected leader must be at least as up-to-date as a majority of the previous configuration
unknowns: Whether the election restriction always keeps truncation above every committed configuration index is argued from source reading rather than established by execution.

behaviors.protocol_context: Durable authority state: the current term and the vote cast in it.
behaviors.trigger: a term change or a decision to grant/vote
implementation_guards: setCurrentTerm panics if the StableStore write fails
persistVote writes the term then the candidate, and its error aborts the operation that needed it

behaviors.protocol_context: Client commands are submitted as futures and completed when the outcome is known.
behaviors.trigger: a client call with an optional timeout
implementation_guards: an enqueue timeout returns ErrEnqueueTimeout without a log entry
a non-leader answers ErrNotLeader
leadership loss answers ErrLeadershipLost and a user restore answers ErrAbortedByRestore
important_branches: deferError.respond ignores a second response, so a future cannot complete twice
async_boundaries: completion is delivered from the FSM or main loop goroutine
existing_protections: ErrLeadershipLost prevents the caller from assuming a write was applied when leadership changed

behaviors.execution_owner: Raft.GetConfiguration with configurationsFuture, callable off the main loop; Raft.Stats() is a second caller
behaviors.protocol_context: A caller reads the cluster's latest configuration and its index in order to order or fence a later configuration change (for example the prevIndex of the next membership change) or to reason about membership freshness.

implementation_guards: the configuration value is served from an atomic copy refreshed by setLatestConfiguration, so the read does not need the main loop
the configurationsCh path used by snapshot creation fills both the configuration and its index from a main-loop clone
external_effects: the returned ConfigurationFuture's Configuration() and Index()

behaviors.execution_owner: RecoverCluster, an offline operator-invoked function that never starts a Raft instance
behaviors.protocol_context: An operator rebuilds one node's stored state from a snapshot plus the log tail when quorum is lost, forcing a chosen configuration instead of a log-recorded change.
behaviors.trigger: a direct call to RecoverCluster with an explicit Configuration and an FSM the caller must discard afterwards
legal_preconditions: existing state is present, as HasExistingState reports
implementation_guards: refuses to run when there is no initial state, so a fresh cluster cannot be created by accident
fails when none of the listed snapshots can be restored
applies only LogCommand entries to the FSM while scanning the log past the snapshot
writes: a new snapshot carrying the supplied configuration at configuration index 1
deletion of the whole stored log range
durable_effects: the new snapshot becomes the recoverable state and the log is left empty
external_effects: the caller's FSM is left holding the recovered state and must be discarded
important_branches: the full log range from first to last index is deleted so that stored configuration entries cannot interfere with the forced configuration
lastIndex and lastTerm are taken from every scanned entry, not only from commands

cross_activity_effects.A4: the supplied configuration is installed as if it had been committed at index 1, bypassing the configuration-change protocol entirely

existing_protections: the entry point refuses to act without existing state and requires a validated configuration
the recovered state is rebuilt from a snapshot plus the command entries of the log tail

on the next start the configuration is installed from the recovered snapshot with the same index for both the latest and the committed configuration, so the one-uncommitted-configuration gate is not confused by the forced configuration index
unknowns: Whether a caller that fences a later change on the recovered configuration index can be misled is not established, because that index is a forced value rather than the index of a real entry.

facts.meaning: A log index in the leader's current term becomes the leader's commitIndex only once a quorum of the voters of the latest configuration is known to hold the log through that index, and never below the first index appended in the leader's current term.

identity.scope: current leader term with the latest configuration's voter set

facts.validity_context: Valid while this server is the leader for its current term; the commitment structure is recreated on becoming leader and discarded on step-down.
facts.durability: The commit index itself is in-memory; the durable consequence is the applied FSM state.
facts.recovery: After restart the commit index is rebuilt from the snapshot and log, and the quorum tracking is rebuilt only when a server becomes leader again.
unknowns: Whether every permitted sequence of one-at-a-time configuration changes keeps a quorum of the latest configuration intersecting a quorum of the committed one is not established by execution.

facts.meaning: The current term is durable and non-decreasing, and a server grants at most one vote per term, only to a candidate whose log is at least as up to date as its own.

identity.object: current term and the vote recorded for it

facts.validity_context: Holds across restarts because the term and the vote are persisted in the StableStore before being relied on.
facts.durability: Written to StableStore; setCurrentTerm panics on write failure and persistVote returns an error that aborts the caller.
facts.recovery: NewRaft reloads CurrentTerm at startup and the last vote is read from StableStore on each RequestVote.

facts.meaning: When a follower accepts an AppendEntries request it keeps a log that agrees with the leader's on all entries up to the request's previous entry, replacing any conflicting suffix, so a reported match index means real agreement.
facts.validity_context: Established per AppendEntries exchange under the current leader term and configuration.
facts.durability: Accepted entries are written to the LogStore before success is reported.
facts.recovery: After restart the prefix is revalidated by the next AppendEntries, and conflicts are removed with DeleteRange.

facts.meaning: The latest configuration is taken from the highest-indexed configuration entry in the log or snapshot and determines the voter set used for quorum, election eligibility and lease checks; the committed configuration is the last one known committed.
facts.validity_context: Valid for the log/snapshot history this server holds; the latest configuration may be uncommitted.
facts.durability: Recovered from the log scan and from a snapshot at startup.
facts.recovery: NewRaft scans configuration entries after the snapshot index and installs the snapshot's configuration.

facts.meaning: Committed entries are applied to the FSM exactly once, in index order and without gaps, up to the last applied index.
facts.validity_context: Per FSM instance; lastApplied only advances and installed snapshots jump it forward.
facts.durability: Depends on the application FSM; the library only guarantees a single ordered application.
facts.recovery: An installed or restored snapshot sets lastApplied to the snapshot index before further entries are applied.
unknowns: Whether the FSM itself persists its effect is application-owned and not established here.

facts.meaning: A server acts as leader only while it holds the leadership for the current term; it abandons that role on observing a higher term or on losing contact with a quorum of current voters.

identity.scope: one term with the latest configuration's voter set

facts.validity_context: Scoped to a term and the latest configuration's voters; not durable across restarts.
facts.durability: Not durable; a restarted server begins again as Follower.
facts.recovery: A restarted node relearns the leader from an AppendEntries request or campaign.

surfaces.reason: The transport heartbeat fast path invokes this handler outside the main loop: NewRaft installs it with trans.SetHeartbeatHandler, and NetworkTransport.handleConn (started with 'go') calls the handler directly for pure heartbeats. Raft.appendEntries is documented as main-thread only, though only pure heartbeats reach it and the fields they touch are individually serialized. The shutdown branch returns without answering the request: an exploration observed the same heartbeat answered immediately while the node ran and unanswered within the observation window after a clean shutdown.
Handles a TimeoutNowRequest by clearing the leader and campaigning; the request's term and sender are not consulted, which is recorded as an open premise of b-leadership-transfer.
Transport-level plumbing that decides whether a request is fast-pathed to the beacon handler or delivered on the consumer channel; it is not itself a consensus obligation.

A separate Go module that replaces github.com/hashicorp/raft with this working copy and pulls a previous release plus an older tag, then exercises mixed-version clusters for rolling upgrades and pre-vote behaviour; it is test scaffolding for the library rather than a runtime protocol responsibility.

The offline recovery entry point has now been read: RecoverCluster refuses to run without existing state, restores the newest usable snapshot, applies the command entries of the log tail, writes a new snapshot carrying the supplied configuration at configuration index 1, and deletes the whole stored log range so stored configuration entries cannot interfere; BootstrapCluster remains the fresh-cluster seeding path.

formation.explanation: The leader appends each accepted command as a local log entry for its term (b-dispatch-logs), then each per-peer replication goroutine pushes AppendEntries and reports the highest index the peer has stored (b-leader-replicate). commitment.match/recalculate turn those per-voter match indexes into a quorum index, refusing to commit anything below the first index appended in the leader's term (b-commit-quorum). When the quorum index advances, the leader loop publishes the new commit index and applies the committed prefix (b-leader-commit-apply). The support is 'qualified' because a match index only counts after the follower's log has been shown to agree with the leader's up to the previous entry.

context.explanation: Authority is scoped to a term and to the voter set of the latest configuration. A follower that stops hearing a leader becomes a candidate (b-heartbeat-timeout); the candidate proposes and persists the next term and asks for votes, optionally after a pre-vote round (b-candidate-election, b-prevote), and becomes leader only on a quorum of current voters. Voters decide with term, membership, an already-persisted vote for the term, and log up-to-date-ness (b-vote-grant). A leader abandons the role when it observes a higher term or cannot contact a quorum of current voters (b-leader-stepdown), and it can hand the role over deliberately with a replicated-then-TimeoutNow transfer (b-leadership-transfer).

connection.explanation: A1 and A2 meet on three sourced points. First, the term-start-index rule in the commitment makes the leader's own new-term entry a precondition for committing anything, so a server that merely won an election cannot commit an earlier leader's entries (b-commit-quorum / f-commit-quorum / f-term-vote). Second, the voter set that defines both a winning quorum and the commitment quorum comes from the latest configuration, so membership changes reshape eligibility and commitment together (b-config-change, b-candidate-election / f-config-membership). Third, a follower only counts as support after its log prefix has been shown to match the leader's, and that same AppendEntries handling carries the term/state transitions; losing the term (b-leader-stepdown) discards the commitment that the old term's support created, while a transfer pushes the target to the leader's last index before handing over. Old work is handled by failing every inflight future with ErrLeadershipLost on step-down, so pending client requests cannot be mistaken for applied decisions.

open_details: The heartbeat fast path (Raft.processHeartbeat, installed by NewRaft and dispatched from NetworkTransport.handleConn) runs appendEntries off the main loop for pure heartbeats; the fields touched are atomic or lock-protected but the ordering against the main loop is unverified.
Raft.timeoutNow campaigns on the target without consulting the request term or sender.
The membership-change error path in appendConfigurationEntry continues to publish the new latest configuration and commitment after a StoreLogs failure that already set state Follower.
core_overview.rationale: Both core lines are read end to end from the leader's append/commit path and from the follower/candidate/voter/step-down path, and their three concrete connections (term-start-index commitment rule, configuration-driven quorum, prefix-validated support with pending-work failure on step-down) are sourced. The remaining items are local anomalies rather than unexplained formation or authority transitions, so the overview is usable while those leads stay open.
